title: A coordinate sufficiently far from constants has no pth root
statement: Let $k\subseteq K$ be complete fields with compatible nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute values, with $k$ algebraically closed [def-weil-field]. Put $F^\circ=\{x\in F:|x|\le1\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring], $\widetilde F=F^\circ/\{x:|x|<1\}$ and $\Gamma_F=|F^\times|$ for $F=k,K$. Assume $\widetilde K=\widetilde k$ and $\Gamma_K=\Gamma_k$. For $u\in K$ let $k(u)^\wedge$ be the closure of the subfield generated by $k$ and $u$. Let $p=\operatorname{char}\widetilde k>0$, and let $z\in K\setminus k$ satisfy $K=k(z)^\wedge$. If $|pz|<\inf_{c\in k}|z-c|$, then there is no $u\in K$ with $u^p=z$.

source.place: Lemma 6.2.8, printed p. 45, specialized to algebraically closed k; the preceding completed tensor product disc description supplies its notation.

proof.text: Put $r=\inf_{c\in k}|z-c|$. The strict hypothesis gives $r>0$. This infimum is not attained. Indeed, if $|z-c|=r$ for some $c\in k$, equality of the value groups supplies $b\in k^\times$ with $|b|=r$. The element $(z-c)/b$ has norm one. Equality of the residue fields supplies $e\in k^\circ$ with $|(z-c)/b-e|<1$. Then $c+be\in k$ and $|z-(c+be)|<r$, a contradiction. Thus $|z-c|>r$ for every $c\in k$.

source.place: Section 6.2, type 4 discussion on pp. 42 and 44; elementary verification of the unattained-distance hypothesis from immediacy.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-analytic-disc-translation-embedding]: the fields are complete, $k$ is algebraically closed, $z\notin k$, $K$ is the closure of $k(z)$, and step 1 verifies both conditions on $r$. Obtain $j:K\to D_r(K)$. Suppose $u^p=z$ and write $j(u)=F=\sum_{n\geq0}a_nW^n$. Since $j$ is a unital algebra homomorphism, $F^p=j(z)=z+W$. Its isometry gives $\|F\|_r^p=|u|^p=|z|$.

source.place: Printed p. 45, completed tensor product disc description preceding Lemma 6.2.8, and its proof; take l=K.

proof.text: In the Cauchy product of $p$ copies of $F$, a term of degree one chooses degree one in exactly one factor and degree zero in all others. Hence the coefficient of $W$ in $F^p$ is $p a_0^{p-1}a_1$. Comparing with $z+W$ gives $p a_0^{p-1}a_1=1$. By the defining supremum norm, $|a_0|\leq\|F\|_r$ and $|a_1|r\leq\|F\|_r$. Multiplying these inequalities yields $r=|p a_0^{p-1}a_1|r\leq |p|\|F\|_r^p=|pz|<r$, a contradiction. The computation is valid in equal characteristic as well: then $p=0$ in $K$, so already the coefficient equality is impossible.

source.place: Lemma 6.2.8, printed p. 45: elementary coefficient formulation of its disc-algebra contradiction.

The item's statement is unchanged. Step 1: r>0 follows from |pz|<r. If the infimum were attained, the equal value groups give b in k with |b|=r and the equal residue fields give e with |z-(c+be)|<r, a contradiction; so |z-c|>r for every c. Step 2: every hypothesis of the new node matches the item. From u^p=z we get F^p=z+W, and the isometry gives ||F||^p=|z| using only multiplicativity in K. Step 3: the W-coefficient of F^p is p a_0^{p-1} a_1=1. With |a_0|<=||F|| and |a_1|r<=||F|| this gives r<=|p||z|<r. In equal characteristic the identity reads 0=1, and p=2 is covered. New node lem-trf-analytic-disc-translation-embedding: I proved it independently. z is transcendental over k, so P(z)->P(z+W) is well defined. Each factor (z-c)+W has Gauss norm |z-c| because |z-c|>r, and it is invertible by a geometric series. The weighted Gauss norm is multiplicative, so the map is an isometry on k(z), and it extends to the completion K because D_r(K) is complete.
